domains.name: Dashboard RBAC
domains.promise: Dashboard access is least-privilege: the guild owner always holds full access, the five seeded system roles (owner, admin, moderator, support, finance) and custom roles grant only their declared dashboard permissions, every route and API call is gated by its mapped permission, priority escalation is impossible, and permission checks fail closed when dependencies are unavailable.

controls.description: Default priority assigned to newly created custom dashboard roles, kept well below the admin (80) and owner (100) system priorities.
Maximum number of dashboard permissions a single custom role may declare, matching the rbacRoleCreate validation limit.
How the dashboard treats routes that have no entry in ROUTE_PERMISSIONS: deny (least-privilege) or allow.
Whether assigning a role with priority above the assigner's own highest role is blocked.

defaults.rationale: Matches the dashboard rbacRoleCreate schema default and keeps new custom roles subordinate to every system role.
Matches the zod validation cap on the /api/rbac/roles create and update schemas.
Least-privilege owner decision: an unmapped route must never be silently reachable by a limited team member.
A team member must never be able to hand out more power than they hold themselves; this guard is not disableable.

permissions.actor: Guild owner signed in through Discord OAuth
permissions.action: Access every dashboard route and API with dashboard.full_access
permissions.enforcement: getAuthContext grants dashboard.full_access when guild.owner_discord_id matches the session's Discord ID.

permissions.action: Create, update, and delete dashboard roles and assign or remove user role assignments via /api/rbac/roles and /api/rbac/users
permissions.enforcement: requirePermission('dashboard.manage_team') guards every /api/rbac handler; writes pass checkAdminRateLimit.

permissions.actor: Team member whose highest role priority is below the target role's priority
permissions.action: Assign a dashboard role with priority above their own
permissions.enforcement: POST /api/rbac/users compares the target role's priority and is_system flag against the caller's highest priority and rejects escalation with 403.

permissions.actor: Authenticated Discord user holding no dashboard role in the guild
permissions.action: Open permission-gated dashboard routes such as /audit, /incidents, or /settings/team
permissions.enforcement: hasRouteAccess and requirePermission fail closed with 401/403; dashboard.full_access is granted only to the owner.

messages.defaultTemplate: You need the {permission} permission to open this part of {guild-name}'s dashboard. Ask your server owner to grant it.

domains.name: Team management
domains.promise: The owner builds a dashboard team through consent-based invitations: a member is invited to a specific dashboard role, is notified by DM with a clear accept path, gains permissions only upon acceptance, and every invitation expires, can be revoked, and is fully audited.

controls.description: How long a pending dashboard-team invitation remains acceptable before it expires.
Whether the invitee receives a Discord DM with the invitation and accept path in addition to seeing it on dashboard sign-in.
Maximum number of simultaneously pending invitations per guild.
Whether a manage_team user may assign a dashboard role directly without the invitee accepting an invitation first.

defaults.rationale: 72 hours balances giving invitees real time to respond against not leaving privileged grants dangling.
Notification parity: an invitation is time-sensitive, so it mirrors to Discord DM as well as the dashboard.
Generous for real teams while capping the blast radius of a compromised manage_team account.
Owner decision: team membership is invitation-based, so permissions are never granted without the member's consent.

domains.name: Automations
domains.promise: Owners compose trigger, condition, and action automations that are powerful but guarded: every rule can be previewed before it goes live, execution is durable and exactly-once per event occurrence, loops are cut at a hard chain depth, per-user rate limits and a mass-action guard contain runaway or compromised-admin rules, and every execution is logged with its outcome.

controls.description: Maximum depth of automation chain reactions before an event is dropped to prevent infinite loops.
Global cap on automation fires per member per minute, enforced atomically in Valkey.
Minimum seconds between automation-sent DMs to the same member from the same automation.
Maximum number of members one automation occurrence may affect before it is held for owner confirmation, containing compromised-admin mass actions.
Whether a new or edited automation must show a dry-run preview of its resolved actions before it can be enabled.

defaults.rationale: Matches AUTOMATION_LIMITS.MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH; three hops covers legitimate cascades while cutting loops fast.
Matches AUTOMATION_LIMITS.MAX_FIRES_PER_USER_PER_MINUTE; generous for real activity, hostile to spam.
Matches AUTOMATION_LIMITS.DM_COOLDOWN_SECONDS; members are never DM-flooded by rules.
A single occurrence touching more than 25 members is almost never intended; holding it protects against harmful loops and compromised admins.
Owner decision: rules preview their resolved actions before going live so surprises happen in the preview, not in the server.

permissions.action: Create, preview, edit, enable, disable, and delete automations via the /automations dashboard and /api/automations
permissions.enforcement: The /automations route and API are gated on dashboard.manage_automations with write rate limiting and zod validation.

permissions.action: View or modify any automation definition or execution log
permissions.enforcement: Route guard plus API permission check return 403; automation internals are never exposed to members.

permissions.action: Execute enabled automations' actions within scope, rate, and guard limits
permissions.enforcement: The engine only loads enabled rows for its own guild, checks scope filters, Valkey rate limits, chain depth, and the mass-action guard before acting.

messages.defaultTemplate: Automation {automation-name} on {guild-name} hit an error: {error}. It stays enabled and will retry safely.

messages.defaultTemplate: Held automation {automation-name}: it tried to affect {member-count} members at once, above your {threshold} guardrail. Approve or edit it from the dashboard.

domains.name: Custom commands
domains.promise: Owners create real guild slash commands from the dashboard that are safe by construction: replies never parse mass mentions, role and channel restrictions gate use, cooldowns are enforced atomically, commands survive restarts through the single bulk registration, and every command is strictly guild-scoped.

controls.description: Per-user cooldown between invocations of the same custom command.
Whether the command's replies are ephemeral (visible only to the invoker) instead of public.
Whether custom-command output suppresses mention parsing so admin templates can never mass-ping.
Maximum number of enabled custom commands loaded per guild.

defaults.rationale: Commands feel instant out of the box; owners add cooldowns per command when a command grants roles or pings channels.
Public replies make commands feel alive in the community by default; owners flip to ephemeral per command for utility commands.
allowedMentions parse is always empty in command output so a template containing @everyone can never mass-ping; this is not disableable.
Matches the loader query limit; effectively unlimited for real guilds while bounding registry memory.

domains.name: Server sync
domains.promise: The guild's live Discord layout is continuously compared against the owner's saved desired state: external changes to roles, channels, permissions, and role hierarchy are detected as drift within the sync interval or via live events, each drift item can be repaired back to the design or accepted as the new design, and repairs are safe, per-item, and never touch @everyone unless explicitly allowed.

controls.description: Whether the periodic sync engine and event-based drift detection run for the guild.
Minutes between periodic sync cycles that snapshot the guild and diff it against the desired state.
Whether detected drift is repaired automatically instead of waiting for a per-item decision on the Sync page.
Whether auto-repair may modify the @everyone role's permissions; kept separate because @everyone changes affect every member.

defaults.rationale: Drift detection is core to the deployed-design promise, so it watches from day one.
Hourly cycles catch anything event listeners missed without hammering the Discord API; live events cover the urgent cases.
Member-respectful guardrail: the owner reviews drift and repairs per item by default; one toggle turns on hands-free repair.
@everyone permission changes affect every member, so silent automatic reversion requires explicit opt-in.

permissions.action: View drift status, trigger repair, accept, or ignore drift items, and update sync configuration
permissions.enforcement: The /sync page maps to dashboard.manage_server; /api/sync validates actions with a discriminated union schema and rate-limits writes.

permissions.action: View or act on drift status and sync configuration
permissions.enforcement: API and route guards return 401/403; drift details are never exposed to unprivileged sessions.

permissions.action: Apply repair actions to Discord entities to restore the desired state
permissions.enforcement: Repairs run only for declared drift items in the bot's own guild, honor the @everyone guard, and emit audit events.

messages.trigger: A sync cycle or live event detects drift from the desired state
messages.surface: Owner notification channel mirror and Sync page
messages.defaultTemplate: Sync check on {guild-name}: {drift-count} item(s) drifted from your saved design ({critical-count} critical). Review them on the Sync page.

messages.surface: Dashboard toast and owner notification mirror
messages.defaultTemplate: Repaired {repaired-count} drift item(s) on {guild-name}; {accepted-count} accepted as the new desired state.

messages.trigger: A repair action fails, for example because the bot's role sits below the target role
messages.surface: Dashboard error state and owner notification mirror
messages.defaultTemplate: Could not repair {entity-name} on {guild-name}: {error}. The drift item stays listed for another try.

values.description: The live guild matches the desired state; no open drift items exist.
One or more drift items are recorded and awaiting repair, accept, or ignore decisions.
Repair actions are being applied to Discord entities.
The sync engine cannot complete a cycle or repair, for example due to Discord API errors or missing permissions.

transitions.expectedEffect: A debounced drift item records the entity, drift type, and observed difference; the owner is alerted.

transitions.trigger: The owner clicks repair (or auto-repair is enabled)
transitions.expectedEffect: The engine applies only the targeted item's correction to Discord.

transitions.expectedEffect: The drift item stays open with the error attached; nothing else is modified.

transitions.trigger: The next cycle or a manual retry runs successfully
transitions.expectedEffect: Open items are re-evaluated; resolved external causes clear naturally.

failures.trigger: The bot's highest role sits below the drifted role, so Discord rejects the repair
failures.expectedBehavior: The repair fails cleanly for that single item, the error names the hierarchy cause, no other entity is touched, and the item remains open.

failures.trigger: Auto-repair encounters @everyone permission drift while auto-repair-everyone is false
failures.expectedBehavior: The item is surfaced for manual decision instead of silently repaired; every other eligible item still auto-repairs.

evidence.expectedObservation: External renames, permission edits, deletions, and hierarchy moves are detected, and repairs restore the exact prior values.

evidence.observer: guild_desired_state and guild_config rows in Supabase
evidence.expectedObservation: Drift details and sync configuration are guild-scoped; accepting drift updates the desired state atomically.

evidence.observer: audit_logs sync category with correlation ids
evidence.expectedObservation: drift.detected, sync.started, sync.completed, and sync.failed rows exist with counts and correlation ids per cycle.

evidence.expectedObservation: Drift detection and repair outcomes mirror to the owner exactly once per condition, debounced across bursts.

evidence.observer: Sync page and notification copy
evidence.expectedObservation: Drift and repair copy renders in the owner voice with subtle powered-by-SomniBot attribution.

evidence.observer: Discord entity state and drift rows under repeated repair requests
evidence.expectedObservation: Repairing an already-repaired item is a no-op; repeated cycles never oscillate an entity between states.
